results.title: USA Annual NLCD - Fractional Impervious Surface
results.description:
Beta Notice: This item is currently in beta and is intended for early access, testing, and feedback. It is not recommended for production use, as functionality and content are subject to change without notice.

Impervious surfaces are surfaces that do not allow water to pass through. Examples of these surfaces include highways, parking lots, rooftops, and airport runways. Instead of allowing rain to pass into the soil, impervious surfaces cause water to collect at the surface, then run off. An increase in impervious surface area causes an increase of water volume which needs to be managed by stormwater systems. With the flow come pollutants, which collect on impervious surfaces then discharge with the runoff into streams and the ocean. Runoff water does not enter the water table, and that can cause other management issues, such as interruptions in baseline stream flow.

The Annual NLCD Fractional Impervious Surface layer serves the percentage of each pixel that is covered with artificial substrate or structures (pavement, concrete, rooftops, and other constructed materials) that are assumed to be impermeable to water. The layer serves a 0-100 continuous value representing a percentage, but the representation of the continuous values is cartographically grouped in the default processing template into a few classes for better understanding. A value of zero represents no mapped impervious surface on the landscape.

Additional information about these annual NLCD layers may be found in the USGS Science Product User Guide.

Dataset Summary
Phenomenon Mapped: The percentage of a pixel that is covered by an impervious surface.
Geographic Extent: Contiguous USA (lower 48 states + DC)
Mosaic Projection: Albers Equal Area Conic, on WGS84 spheroid (AEA_WGS84)
Data Coordinate System: Albers Equal Area Conic, on WGS84 spheroid (AEA_WGS84)
Cell Size: 30 meters
Pixel Depth: 8 Bit Unsigned
Source Type: Thematic
Time Extent: Annually 1985-2024
Analysis: Analysis-Optimized
Update Frequency: Annually
Source: National Land Cover Database, Multi-Resolution Land Characteristics Consortium 
Data Vintage: Version 1.1, June 25, 2025
Publication Date: 2025

What can you do with this layer?
Model changes in infiltration vs runoff over time.
Display a time series to show changes in hardscape due to development.

Read the Explore 40 Years of Analysis-Ready Annual NLCD Landcover blog. 

Analysis

  • In order to leverage the optimization for analysis, the capability must be enabled by your ArcGIS organization administrator. More information on enabling this feature can be found in the ‘Regional data hosting’ section of this help doc.
  • Optimized for analysis means this layer does not have size constraints for analysis and it is recommended for multisource analysis with other layers optimized for analysis. See the ArcGIS Living Atlas: Analysis-Optimized Imagery Layers Group for a complete list of imagery layers optimized for analysis. 

Processing Templates
Impervious Surface Cool Renderer - Displays imperviousness in a few cool gray classes suitable for dark and light backgrounds. Even though the data appears grouped/classified in a map to aid user understanding, the original pixel value from 0-100 (percent impervious) is available and may be used in analysis.
Impervious Surface Warm Renderer - Displays imperviousness in a few warm orange classes suitable for dark and light backgrounds. Even though the data appears grouped/classified in a map to aid user understanding, the original pixel value from 0-100 (percent impervious) is available and may be used in analysis.
Impervious Surface USGS Default Renderer - Displays imperviousness as a continuous ramp of values per specifications of USGS, the data producer. 

Questions?
Please leave a comment below if you have a question about this layer, and we will get back to you as soon as possible.

results.title: US Land Cover Impervious Surface
results.description:
Overview

This image service provides a national mosaic dataset of annual fractional impervious surface across the United States. It delivers thematic raster data as a single-band uint8 service with 30 meter cell size in Albers equal area projection. The coverage spans the contiguous United States and supports viewing and analysis of developed surface percentages for each mapped year.

The service includes raster rendering options for cool, warm, and USGS default impervious surface display styles.

Temporal summary: The catalog is time-aware and covers a historical time series from annual records beginning in 1985 through 2024. Users can filter by year and explore change in impervious surface over time.

Geographic coverage: United States national extent.

Raster Properties
  • Data type: Thematic
  • Pixel type: uint8
  • Band count: 1
  • Band name: Band 1
  • Cell size: 30 meters
  • Dataset format: AMD
  • Default resampling: Nearest
  • Compression: None
  • Maximum image size: 20,000 by 20,000 pixels
Mosaic Properties

The service is built from a mosaic dataset and presents an image collection of annual raster items that are mosaicked on the fly. The default mosaic method is Northwest, with supported methods including Center, Lock Raster, By Attribute, Nadir, Viewpoint, Seamline, and None. The mosaic operator is First, and up to 20 images can be composited at once.

Catalog fields provide item metadata including name, category, tag, group name, product name, center coordinates, year, version, and start and end dates. The category field includes coded values such as Primary, Overview, Inactive, and Uploaded.

Use Cases

This service supports image export, metadata access, catalog browsing, and basic mensuration. It also supports copy and analysis. Catalog queries support statistics, ordering, pagination, and distinct values, with a maximum of 1,000 records per response.

These capabilities support inspection of impervious surface patterns, annual change monitoring, and map display for national-scale land development analysis.
